newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian rebels kill four soldiers, take prisoners.
newsitem.headline: Colombian rebels kill four soldiers, take prisoners.

text.p: Leftist rebels killed at least four Colombian marines and took eight others prisoner on Thursday in an attack in northwestern Choco province, government and military officials said.
At least one marine was officially listed as missing after the attack and eight others were wounded, a statement from the presidential press office said.
It said the attack, on a drug and arms checkpoint in the Pacific coast municipality of Jurado, was carried out by Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels.

The FARC, Colombia's largest and oldest rebel group, took at least 60 other prisoners in an attack last August on a military base in a jungle-covered area of southwestern Putumayo province. Twenty-seven soldiers were killed in that attack, which marked the start of a nationwide rebel offensive, and the prisoners are still being held.
The FARC, which specialises in kidnappings and the protection of rural drug operations, was founded as a Marxist, pro-Soviet group in 1964.
